name: Bungee and Canyon Swing Adventure
region: Sindhupalchok (Bhote Koshi gorge) and Parbat/Baglung (Kali Gandaki gorge)
sub_region: The Last Resort, Sindhupalchok District, Bagmati Province; The Cliff, Kushma, Parbat District, Gandaki Province

difficulty.notes: No experience needed; physically brief but psychologically intense. Weight limits apply (Kushma bungee 45-100 kg; Kushma swing 40-145 kg; Last Resort swing max 120 kg per one guide).

duration_days.basis: day trip from Kathmandu (The Last Resort) or from Pokhara (Kushma)
duration_days.notes: The Last Resort is ~3-4 h each way from Kathmandu and offers tented overnight stays, canyoning and Bhote Koshi rafting; Kushma is ~57-60 km (~2-3 h) from Pokhara.

itinerary.route: Kathmandu - Araniko Highway - The Last Resort (100 km, ~3-4 h) - 160 m bungee and/or canyon swing from the suspension bridge over the Bhote Koshi - return to Kathmandu or stay overnight
itinerary.notes: The Last Resort operates Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Pokhara-based alternative: drive to Kushma for the 228 m bungee / swing.

best_seasons.notes: Operates year-round weather permitting; heavy rain or high winds pause jumps. Monsoon road conditions to the Bhote Koshi can be poor.

guide_requirements: No permit; activities run by the site operators (The Last Resort; The Cliff Nepal at Kushma) with their jump masters.

drives: Kathmandu - The Last Resort, 100 km on the Araniko Highway toward Tatopani, ~3-4 h
logistics.notes: The Last Resort location: Naya Pul near Tatopani, Sindhupalchok; sales office in Thamel. Kushma site is ~500 m from Kushma bazaar.

highlights: The Last Resort: Nepal's first bungee, a 160 m jump to the Bhote Koshi from a steel suspension bridge, designed by New Zealand bungee consultants (operating since ~1998)
The Last Resort canyon swing: 160 m high, 100 m freefall, 240 m arc, ~150 km/h
Kushma (The Cliff): 228 m bungee over the Kali Gandaki gorge from a 520 m bridge linking Parbat and Baglung; opened October 2020
Kushma swing at 228 m (marketed as the world's highest swing), plus sky cycling
Combine with Bhote Koshi rafting or canyoning at The Last Resort
risks: Inherent risk of extreme activities; medical contraindications (heart, back, pregnancy etc.)
Mountain road travel and landslides in monsoon
unverified: Bridge dimension at The Last Resort: NTB calls it a '166 m wide' suspension bridge; some operators say it 'hangs 166 m' above the river. The jump height of 160 m is consistent.
Kushma as 'world's second-highest bungee' and 'world's highest swing' are operator marketing claims.
Kushma swing freefall: 8.5 s (site) vs ~6 s (another operator); Last Resort swing freefall ~7 s (operator blog).
2026 operating status: The Last Resort website lists 4 operating days a week; impact (if any) of the Aug-Sep 2026 floods on access roads not confirmed.
